2609.25303.title: Potential for Enhanced Learning in Machine Learning Classes by Using Wiki LLM Indexing
2609.25303.paper_summary: Large language models are increasingly deployed as course-specific tutors, but their usefulness depends on grounding in vetted instructional materials that are often revised mid-semester. Our prior work built a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system over an authentic machine learning course corpus (Foundations of Machine Learning) and found that retrieval improved contextual grounding, but that fixed retrieval strategies were suboptimal. That motivates a different question: whether how a corpus is structured at ingest time matters more than how much is retrieved at query time. We present a controlled head-to-head comparison of two knowledge representations over an identical classroom corpus: (A) vector RAG, replicating the best-performing configuration from our prior study, and (B) an LLM-compiled wiki (Karpathy framework), in which the corpus is synthesized at ingest into linked concept pages with explicit cross-references and citations back to source materials. We evaluate 59 questions spanning single-fact recall, cross-unit concept linking, synthesis and explanation, and currency after a syllabus revision, scored by an LLM judge against a human-authored rubric. Both representations answered single-fact questions about equally well (9.33 vs. 9.96 of 10), but diverged sharply on questions requiring links across course units. The compiled wiki remained accurate and grounded (9.93; 100% grounded in cited sources), while retrieval scored lower and was markedly less grounded (8.14; 64%). The wiki's citations let students and instructors trace any claim back to the lecture that introduced it, adding a layer of dynamic retrieval that machine learning courses require. While further testing is needed, instructors using AI to support learning in ML courses should consider wiki-based structure for its potential to support foundational elements of best practice.
2609.25303.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型越來越多地被用作課程特定的輔導工具，但它們的有效性取決於基於經過審核的教學材料的基礎，這些材料通常在學期中進行修訂。我們之前的研究建立了一個多模態檢索增強生成（RAG）系統，基於一個真實的機器學習課程語料庫（機器學習基礎），並發現檢索改善了上下文基礎，但固定的檢索策略並不理想。這引發了一個不同的問題：在攝取時語料庫的結構是否比查詢時檢索的數量更為重要。我們對兩種知識表示法進行了受控的對比，使用相同的課堂語料庫：（A）向量 RAG，複製了我們之前研究中表現最佳的配置，以及（B）一個 LLM 編譯的維基（Karpathy 框架），其中語料庫在攝取時合成為帶有明確交叉引用和回溯來源材料的鏈接概念頁面。我們評估了59個問題，涵蓋單一事實回憶、跨單元概念鏈接、綜合與解釋，以及在課程大綱修訂後的時效性，並由 LLM 評審根據人類撰寫的標準進行評分。兩種表示法對單一事實問題的回答表現相當（9.33 vs. 9.96 的 10），但在需要跨課程單元鏈接的問題上卻有明顯的分歧。編譯的維基保持了準確性和基礎性（9.93；100% 基於引用來源），而檢索的得分較低且明顯缺乏基礎（8.14；64%）。維基的引用讓學生和教師能夠追溯任何主張到引入它的講座，增加了機器學習課程所需的動態檢索層面。雖然還需要進一步測試，但使用 AI 支持機器學習課程學習的教師應考慮基於維基的結構，以其潛力支持最佳實踐的基礎要素。
2609.25303.author: Brian Wright et.al.
